name: FlashAttention 1-4 generation comparison: what each changed mechanically and measured performance
arithmetic_intensity: Each FA generation attacks a different bottleneck. FA-1 (2022): IO-aware tiling eliminates S x S HBM round trip, 2-4x wallclock vs PyTorch. FA-2 (2023): work partitioning fix, ~2x vs FA-1, 50-73% of peak FLOPs/s on A100 (FA-1 was 25-40%). FA-3 (2024): Hopper warp specialization + TMA + FP8, 1.5-2.0x vs FA-2, 740 TFLOPs/s FP16 (75% of 989 TFLOPS peak), ~1.2 PFLOPs/s FP8 on H100. FA-4 (2025): Blackwell tcgen05 UMMA + TMEM + 2-CTA MMA + emulated exp, up to 1605 TFLOPs/s BF16 on B200 (71% of 2250 TFLOPS peak). The progression: FA-1 fixes bytes, FA-2 fixes scheduling, FA-3 fixes SFU/matmul overlap, FA-4 fixes shared-memory bandwidth in backward. Each generation is arch-specific: FA-1 works on Ampere+, FA-2 adds better Ampere/Ada, FA-3 requires Hopper (wgmma + TMA), FA-4 requires Blackwell (tcgen05 + TMEM).
scales_with: precision (FA-3 FP8 doubles tensor-core flops but SFU exp unchanged)
num_SMs (FA-2 partitioning, FA-4 2-CTA MMA needs CTA pairs)
workarounds: FA-1: tiling with online softmax, recompute S in backward instead of storing
FA-2: parallelize over batch*seqlen*heads, reduce non-matmul FLOPs, better warp distribution
FA-3: warp specialization (producer TMA + consumer WGMMA), ping-pong warpgroups, 2-stage pipelining, FP8 with incoherent processing (Hadamard transform)
FA-4: tcgen05 UMMA with TMEM accumulators, 2-CTA MMA halving operand-B SMEM traffic, emulated exp (Cody-Waite + Horner polynomial on FMA), conditional online-softmax rescaling, LPT tile scheduling
notes:
Measured performance summary (all author-reported): FA-1: 2-4x vs PyTorch, 25-40% peak. FA-2: ~2x vs FA-1, 50-73% peak on A100, 225 TFLOPs/s training (72% MFU). FA-3: 1.5-2.0x vs FA-2, 740 TFLOPs/s FP16 (75%), ~1.2 PFLOPs/s FP8 on H100. FA-4: 1605 TFLOPs/s BF16 on B200 (71%), 1.3x vs cuDNN 9.13, 2.7x vs Triton. Key insight: the bottleneck migrates from HBM bytes (FA-1) to scheduling (FA-2) to SFU/matmul overlap (FA-3) to shared-memory bandwidth (FA-4). On Hopper, SFU throughput is 3.9 TFLOPS vs 989 TFLOPS matmul, so at head_dim 128 exp() can consume ~50% of step time. FA-3 reduces register pressure to address this. FA-4 moves bottleneck to SMEM bandwidth in backward (3328 SMEM cycles vs 2560 tensor-core cycles per tile). Sources: arXiv 2205.14135, 2307.08691, 2407.08608, 2501.09294.
